EnergyManagementPage.leadText: Eneplus performs an energy management service that represents the process of managing the energy performance of a municipality, company or specific facility, and includes an analysis of the current state, the process of procurement and energy production until its final use.

Such activities provide long-term continuity and effectiveness of energy efficiency programs.
EnergyManagementPage.isoSubtitle: The energy management cycle according to the ISO 50001 standard implies the implementation of the following activities:

Implementing an energy saving plan through examined and approved projects
Control of the realization of the energy saving plan
Monitoring the effect of the implemented measures
Application of corrective measures in relation to nonconformities and deviations from the plans
Conducting internal audits that verify that the energy management system is well established and in place

EnergyAuditsPage.introText: An energy audit is an inspection, survey and analysis of energy flows, for energy conservation in a building, process or system to reduce the amount of energy input into the system without negatively affecting the output(s).
EnergyAuditsPage.detailsText1: It is the first step in identifying opportunities to reduce energy expense and carbon footprints. It is an efficient tool that gives a clear insight into the condition of power installations, equipment and also the constructive characteristics of the facility that have a significant impact on energy consumption. The aim of the energy audit is to determine the location and causes of irrational energy consumption.
EnergyAuditsPage.detailsText2: By eliminating these causes, we achieve not only energy savings, but also savings in the budget, as well as extending the life of equipment and installations.
EnergyAuditsPage.strategyText: An energy audit is a systematic approach to reviewing the existing energy performance of a system or object, including an analysis of measures to improve its energy efficiency. Energy efficiency becomes a factor of success and the competitive advantage of companies, as energy is the basis of prosperity and economic development.

Advising on the establishment of an energy management system
benefitsList: Improvement of the company / institution image

In addition to providing an insight into the state of the object in terms of thermal insulation of the building, infrared thermography can be successfully applied to assess the condition of the building envelope:

the detection of the separation of the mortar from the surface and the possible presence of air or moisture into the layers below the outer plasters, and for evaluation of flat roofs
detection of the location of the separation of the roofing board from the substrate, inspection of electrical and HVAC installations, inspection of devices and equipment, etc …

EnergyPassportPage.heroSubtitle: Professional energy passport certification for residential, commercial, and public buildings across Serbia. Fast, reliable, and at fair prices.
EnergyPassportPage.introText1: An energy passport (also known as an energy performance certificate) is an official document that contains the calculated annual energy consumption values of a building, its energy rating class (from A+ to G), and professional recommendations for improving energy efficiency.
EnergyPassportPage.introText2: This document is mandatory for all newly constructed buildings, as well as existing structures undergoing reconstruction, adaptation, renovation, or energy rehabilitation – with the exception of buildings specifically exempt from this requirement by law. It constitutes an essential part of the technical documentation submitted when applying for a building usage permit.
EnergyPassportPage.introText3: An energy passport is important not only as a legal requirement, but also as a tool that provides future owners and buyers a clear view of the building's energy efficiency. Based on it, you can precisely estimate the expected heating and cooling costs, which directly impacts the property's market value.
EnergyPassportPage.introText4: Eneplus prepares energy passports for all types of buildings – residential buildings, houses, apartments, commercial spaces, public buildings, and industrial facilities – across the entire territory of Serbia.
EnergyPassportPage.scenario1Title: Building a new property or renovating an existing one?
EnergyPassportPage.scenario1Text: An energy passport is a mandatory step in obtaining a usage permit. Without it, the competent authority will not issue a permit for use of the building – regardless of whether it is a family house, residential building, or commercial space.
EnergyPassportPage.scenario2Title: Selling, buying, or renting out a property?
EnergyPassportPage.scenario2Text: According to the Law on Planning and Construction, every property advertised for sale or lease must have a valid energy passport. The owner is obligated to provide this document before putting the property on the market.
EnergyPassportPage.scenario3Text: Banks in Serbia increasingly require an energy passport as part of mandatory documentation when approving housing loans. This document confirms the energy class of the property and helps the bank assess the long-term value of the property.
EnergyPassportPage.process1Text: Fill out our online form with basic property details or call us by phone. We respond within a few hours.
EnergyPassportPage.process2Text: Send us a copy of the building permit, architectural project, and photos of the building. Documentation can be submitted electronically or in person.
EnergyPassportPage.process3Text: Our licensed engineer visits the location to inspect the building, take measurements, and verify data from the technical documentation.
EnergyPassportPage.process4Text: Based on the collected data, we prepare the energy passport with detailed calculations, energy rating, and recommendations for improving efficiency.
EnergyPassportPage.process5Text: The completed energy passport is delivered in electronic form. A copy is also sent to the relevant ministry in accordance with the law.
EnergyPassportPage.legalText1: Energy certification of buildings in Serbia is regulated by the Law on Planning and Construction and accompanying regulations that precisely define the obligations of owners and investors regarding the energy efficiency of buildings.
EnergyPassportPage.legalHighlight: According to current regulations, an energy passport is mandatory for all new buildings, as well as existing buildings that are being reconstructed, adapted, or energy-renovated. Without an energy passport, it is not possible to obtain a usage permit.
EnergyPassportPage.legalText2: The Regulation on Energy Efficiency of Buildings and the Regulation on Conditions, Content, and Method of Issuing Energy Performance Certificates precisely define the following obligations:
EnergyPassportPage.legalItem1: All newly constructed buildings must have an energy passport before issuance of a usage permit
EnergyPassportPage.legalItem2: Existing buildings undergoing reconstruction, adaptation, or renovation are subject to mandatory energy certification
EnergyPassportPage.legalItem3: When selling or leasing a property, the owner is obligated to present the energy passport to the buyer or tenant
EnergyPassportPage.legalItem4: Energy passports are issued exclusively by authorized entities with licensed engineers of the appropriate profession
EnergyPassportPage.legalItem5: An energy passport is valid for 10 years from the date of issuance, after which it must be renewed
EnergyPassportPage.docsSubtitle: To prepare your energy passport as quickly as possible, please provide the following documentation:
EnergyPassportPage.doc6: Copy of property registry extract (cadastral extract)
EnergyPassportPage.docsNote: * If any of the listed documentation does not exist in electronic form, you can deliver it in person or mention it in the note when submitting the request.
EnergyPassportPage.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about energy passports
EnergyPassportPage.faq1Question: How much does an energy passport cost?
EnergyPassportPage.faq1Answer: The cost of an energy passport depends on the type and size of the building. For apartments and smaller houses, the price ranges from 15,000 to 30,000 dinars, while for larger and more complex buildings, the price may be higher. Contact us for an exact quote tailored to your building – no obligation.
EnergyPassportPage.faq2Question: How long does it take to prepare an energy passport?
EnergyPassportPage.faq2Answer: Energy passport preparation usually takes 2 to 5 business days, depending on the complexity of the building and the completeness of the submitted documentation. In urgent cases, expedited preparation within 24 to 48 hours is also possible.
EnergyPassportPage.faq3Question: Is an energy passport legally required?
EnergyPassportPage.faq3Answer: Yes. According to the Law on Planning and Construction of the Republic of Serbia, an energy passport is mandatory for all newly constructed buildings, as well as existing buildings undergoing reconstruction or adaptation. Without an energy passport, a usage permit cannot be obtained. Additionally, when selling or leasing a property, the owner is required to provide this document.
EnergyPassportPage.faq4Question: How long is an energy passport valid?
EnergyPassportPage.faq4Answer: An energy passport is valid for 10 years from the date of issuance. After the validity period expires, a new energy passport must be prepared if the building is subject to the legal requirement for this document.
EnergyPassportPage.faq5Question: Which buildings are exempt from having an energy passport?
EnergyPassportPage.faq5Answer: The following buildings are exempt from having an energy passport: buildings used for religious ceremonies, temporary buildings used for less than two years, industrial buildings with low energy consumption, freestanding buildings with a useful area of less than 50m², and buildings protected as cultural heritage.
EnergyPassportPage.faq6Question: What does an energy passport contain?
EnergyPassportPage.faq6Answer: An energy passport contains data on the building's energy rating (from A+ to G), calculated annual energy consumption per square meter, data on the thermal envelope and heating/cooling systems, as well as specific recommendations for improving the building's energy efficiency.
EnergyPassportPage.faq7Answer: Yes, a site visit is a mandatory part of the energy passport preparation process. A licensed engineer performs a visual inspection of the building, verifies compliance with project documentation, and takes additional measurements as needed. The visit usually takes 30 minutes to 2 hours, depending on the size of the building.
EnergyPassportPage.faq8Question: Which competent body is responsible for energy passport verification?
EnergyPassportPage.faq8Answer: When an energy passport is issued, checking its regularity and record-keeping is done through the CREP system (Central Register of Energy Passports). There, the ministry strictly inspects all passports issued by licensed companies such as Eneplus. Always pay attention to who you hire and whether they possess a valid license.
EnergyPassportPage.faq9Question: What is the first step if I need an energy passport?
EnergyPassportPage.faq9Answer: It all starts by sending us your basic information. Click on the request form in the top menu. Request an online quote - it's completely obligation-free, and our licensed energy efficiency engineer will contact you to discuss dynamics, documentation, and your exact energy passport price.
EnergyPassportPage.ctaText: Submit your request through our online form or call us by phone. We respond quickly, work professionally, and offer competitive pricing across all of Serbia.

FAQ.title: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.subtitle: Answers to common questions regarding energy efficiency, management, and consulting services
FAQ.q1: What is the price for an energy passport and how long does it take?
FAQ.a1: The cost of an energy passport depends on the size and type of the building. For standard residential properties, the price usually ranges from 15,000 to 30,000 RSD. The preparation typically takes 2 to 5 business days, ensuring a fast and efficient process.
FAQ.q2: Is an energy passport legally required?
FAQ.a2: Yes, according to the Law on Planning and Construction. It is mandatory for all new buildings, as well as existing buildings undergoing reconstruction or adaptation. It is also required when selling or renting out a property.
FAQ.q3: What does the energy management process entail?
FAQ.a3: Energy management is the systematic monitoring and analysis of energy consumption aimed at reducing costs (following ISO 50001). The process includes a detailed energy audit, the development of an energy-saving action plan, and supervision of implemented measures.
FAQ.q4: How do your energy consulting services work?
FAQ.a4: Our energy consulting provides expert advice on optimal solutions for your facility. Simply send us a project description and relevant documentation, and our engineers will analyze and propose the most energy-efficient and cost-effective steps.
FAQ.q5: Why is an energy audit important before renovation?
FAQ.a5: An energy audit deeply analyzes your current condition using state-of-the-art equipment. It precisely locates energy losses before you start renovating, which prevents unnecessary expenses and directs the budget to measures that yield the highest savings.
